title: State the rule of an increasing or decreasing pattern in words and numbers

lesson.title: Say the Pattern Rule Out Loud

steps.say: You already know how to say a pattern rule like start at three, add two each time. Today we will look at a table of numbers and figure out that rule ourselves, so we can say it in words and in numbers.

Here is Maya saving loonies in her piggy bank. Look at the table. In week one she has four dollars, then six, then eight, then ten. To find the rule, ask two little questions. Where did it start? And what happens each jump?

Let us check the jumps. Four to six is a jump of two. Six to eight is a jump of two. Eight to ten is a jump of two. Same jump every time, and the numbers are getting bigger, so this is an increasing pattern. In words the rule is start at four, add two each time. In numbers we write plus two, plus two, plus two.

Now a decreasing one. A snow pile outside the school melts down. On day one it is thirty centimetres tall, then twenty five, then twenty, then fifteen. Thirty minus twenty five is five. Twenty five minus twenty is five. Twenty minus fifteen is five. The numbers are getting smaller by the same amount, so the rule is start at thirty, subtract five each time.

visual.caption: Snow pile shrinking by five centimetres

steps.say: Here is a mix up to watch out for. Some kids look at Maya's table and say the rule is add four, because four is the first number they see. But four is where the pattern starts, not the jump. The starting number and the jump are two different jobs. Always find the start first, then look between the numbers for the jump.

visual.caption: Four is the start, plus two is the jump

steps.say: So every pattern rule needs two pieces. Say where it starts, and say what you do each time. Start at four, add two each time. Start at thirty, subtract five each time.

lesson.answer: A pattern rule has two parts: where it starts, and what you add or subtract each time.

practice.question: Liam is filling a water bottle at the school fountain. The table shows millilitres in the bottle: after one press, one hundred; after two presses, one hundred fifty; after three presses, two hundred; after four presses, two hundred fifty. Say the rule in words and in numbers.
practice.answer: Start at one hundred millilitres, add fifty each time. In numbers: plus fifty, plus fifty, plus fifty. It is an increasing pattern.
